findings.claim: The geometrization target is false as sketched and does not match the theorem that was proved. (i) HasGeometricStructure p G asks for a complete locally homogeneous metric on a JSJ piece p, which is a compact manifold with torus boundary; such a metric modelled on a boundaryless X (equivalently p = X/Γ) cannot exist when ∂p ≠ ∅, so the statement fails for every M with a nonempty JSJ family (every graph manifold). Kirby's own remark puts the structure on int M. (ii) 'Finite volume' is missing, and with it the statement is only true after also cutting along Klein bottles / allowing the exceptional pieces: Morgan-Tian's proved statement cuts along tori and Klein bottles and asks each complementary component for a locally homogeneous metric of finite volume; for a Sol torus bundle the JSJ piece T^2 × I has no finite-volume geometric interior. (iii) The only full-text source cited, Morgan-Tian 'Ricci Flow and the Poincaré Conjecture' (arXiv:math/0607607), proves the Poincaré conjecture only; the completion of geometrization is Morgan-Tian arXiv:0809.4040 (Clay Math. Monographs 5, 2014), or Bessières-Besson-Boileau-Maillot-Porti (EMS Tracts 13, 2010) and Kleiner-Lott (Geom. Topol. 12 (2008)). (iv) The layer says Poincaré 'falls out as an instance', but Mathlib already pins the 3-dimensional Poincaré statements as proof_wanted; deriving them needs the prime decomposition and the classification of spherical space forms, not an instance.

findings.claim: The Levine target for [Kir97, 1.31] is trivially true as written, and it misdescribes the category. 'A knot in a homology sphere not smoothly concordant to any in S^3' holds for every knot in the Poincaré homology sphere, because that sphere (Rokhlin invariant 1) is not homology cobordant to S^3, so no annulus in any homology cobordism exists. Matsumoto's question, and Levine's theorem, concern knots in homology spheres that bound (PL) acyclic 4-manifolds, with concordance taken in homology cobordisms; Levine shows the inclusion C_Z → Ĉ_Z is not surjective, which answers the PL question as posed because a knot bounds a PL disc in some homology ball iff it is homology concordant to a knot in S^3. The layer plans none of: homology 3-spheres, homology cobordisms, homology 4-balls, homology concordance, the groups C_Z and Ĉ_Z; its concordance is defined only in S^3 × [0,1]. The design note calls this 'a small extension'.

findings.claim: The unlock for [Kir97, 1.41] names the wrong paper and the wrong invariant. 1.41(A) (0-shake genus versus slice genus) was resolved by Piccirillo, 'Shake genus and slice genus' (Geom. Topol. 23 (2019) 2665-2684), not by the Conway-knot paper that the references attach to 1.41. The lower bound in both papers is Rasmussen's s-invariant from Khovanov homology, not τ: the shake-genus paper says 'To give lower bounds on g_4(K') we use Rasmussen's s invariant' and notes that whether τ is a 0-trace invariant is unknown; the Conway-knot paper shows τ(K') = 0 for every K' with the same trace, so τ cannot give the argument. No atlas stage plans Khovanov homology or s. Separately, no layer defines the objects of the statement: the knot trace X_0(K) (B^4 with a 0-framed 2-handle), the generator of H_2(X_0(K)), homology classes of embedded surfaces, and the 0-shake genus.

findings.claim: Several Kirby numbers are wrong. (a) Hatcher's Smale conjecture Diff(S^3) ≃ O(4) is labelled [Kir97, 4.34], but 4.34 asks 'What is π_0(Diff(S^4))? Indeed, is Diff(S^4) ≃ O(5)?'; the Smale conjecture is Problem 3.34 (Smale), whose update records Hatcher's proof. Watanabe answers 4.126(C) and the second question of 4.34; the first question of 4.34 (π_0 Diff(S^4)) remains open. (b) Property R is Problem 1.16, not 1.82 (see the next finding for 1.82). (c) The virtual Haken conjecture is Problem 3.2 (Waldhausen), not 3.51; 3.51 is virtual fibering. (d) Manolescu's theorem is recorded as 'no Kirby number', but it answers Problem 4.4 negatively (no homology 3-sphere H of Rokhlin invariant one with H#H bounding a PL acyclic 4-manifold), which is exactly the Galewski-Stern/Matumoto criterion.

findings.claim: [Kir97, 4.82] is listed as a Layer 1 unlock with no source and a wrong gloss, and Layer 1 cannot state it. The problem was answered yes by Ruberman-Stern in 1997: *CP^2 # *RP^4 is smoothable. The gloss 'a smooth structure on a fake RP^4' is wrong: *RP^4 has nonzero Kirby-Siebenmann invariant and is not smoothable; the question is about the connected sum, which has KS = 0. Stating the problem needs the topological manifolds *CP^2 (Freedman's Chern manifold, which needs a contractible topological 4-manifold bounding the Poincaré sphere) and *RP^4 (Hambleton-Kreck-Teichner, by topological surgery), or a characterisation through homotopy type and the Kirby-Siebenmann invariant, which the roadmap defers to its far-horizon section. None of this is in Layer 1 or any other stage.

Chirally cosmetic surgeries themselves were already known when the list was written (Mathieu 1990 on the trefoil exterior; Bleiler-Hodgson-Weeks). findings.claim: The defining relation of Layer 6 is mis-sketched. 'Concordant K K' := ∃ Σ : Annulus (sphere 3 ×ₘ I), boundary Σ = K ⊔ K'.mirror' uses the mirror image, which the Layer 4 convention table defines as reflection negating every crossing. With that reading the relation is not reflexive: the product annulus K × I has boundary K ⊔ K, and a trefoil is not concordant to its mirror (signatures -2 and 2). The annulus should run from K × {0} to K' × {1}, with the reversed string orientation arising from the boundary orientation of S^3 × I, not a mirror.

findings.fix: Define smooth (resp. locally flat) concordance as: there is a smoothly (resp. locally flatly) properly embedded annulus A ⊂ S^3 × [0,1] with A ∩ (S^3 × {0}) = K × {0} and A ∩ (S^3 × {1}) = K' × {1}, oriented so that ∂A = K × {0} ⊔ −(K' × {1}). findings.claim: Layer 1's gluing, handle and connected-sum plans rely on objects it never constructs, and its corners plan is wrong in one claim and too thin for its consumer. (1) The closed ball D^n is never given a smooth manifold-with-boundary structure, with ∂D^n diffeomorphic to Mathlib's sphere; neither library has one, yet connectedSum takes 'Embedding (closedBall n) M', Layer 4 slices in D^4, Layer 5 fills with S^1 × D^2 and Layer 9 builds handlebodies. (2) Handles D^k × D^(n-k), and products of manifolds with boundary generally, are manifolds with corners. Mathlib's product of two half-space models is not its quadrant model, and gluing along a proper face 'produces corners along ∂A', but no straightening-the-angle (corner rounding) step returns the result to a manifold with boundary. (3) The design claim that corners have a 'boundary [that] is again a manifold-with-corners' is false for the subset I.boundary M: the boundary of [0,∞)^2 is a bent line with no compatible structure making the inclusion an immersion. What holds is Joyce's abstract boundary ∂X, a manifold with corners immersed non-injectively, or the individual faces. (4) ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces ALS.2 needs manifolds with corners of arbitrary codimension, collars of corners, and the homotopy equivalence from the interior, from this layer. Layer 1 plans corners only 'afterwards', and ALS.2 records no edge to it.

findings.claim: The isotopy extension theorem is planned nowhere, though Layer 1's connected-sum well-definedness needs it and MordellLawrenceVenkatesh LV.5 lists 'isotopy extension (GeometricTopology Layer 1)' as an input. The cited disc theorem (Hirsch 4.6.6) gives only an isotopy of disc embeddings rel the centre, on a boundaryless manifold. Turning it into the ambient isotopy that transports the connected-sum construction needs Thom-Cerf-Palais isotopy extension, and moving the centre point needs homogeneity of connected manifolds.

findings.claim: The Annulus Conjecture target uses 'inside Σ₁' and 'regionBetween Σ₁ Σ₂' without planning the theorems that define them. These are the Jordan-Brouwer separation theorem for locally flat (n-1)-spheres in ℝ^n or S^n, and the generalized Schoenflies theorem (Brown 1960, Mazur 1959): a bicollared (n-1)-sphere in S^n bounds balls on both sides. Schoenflies is the classical consequence of Brown's bicollaring, which the layer does plan. Neither library has separation or Schoenflies in any dimension (Tau Ceti's conformal-mapping files say Mathlib has no Jordan curve theorem), and no atlas stage plans them. The attribution also omits dimensions 2-3 (Radó, Moise).

findings.fix: Add to Layer 2: (a) Jordan-Brouwer separation for a locally flat (equivalently, by Brown, bicollared) (n-1)-sphere Σ ⊂ S^n: S^n ∖ Σ has exactly two components, each with frontier Σ (via Alexander duality from AlgebraicTopology Stage 6, or Mayer-Vietoris with the bicollar); define inside for Σ ⊂ ℝ^n as the bounded component; (b) the generalized Schoenflies theorem (M. Brown, 'A proof of the generalized Schoenflies theorem', Bull. AMS 66 (1960) 74-76): the closure of each component is a closed n-ball; (c) state the annulus theorem with regionBetween := closure(inside Σ₁) ∖ inside Σ₂, citing Radó (n = 2), Moise (n = 3), Kirby 1969 (n ≥ 5) and Quinn 1982 (n = 4).

findings.claim: The basic 3-manifold notions the Layer 7-10 statements rest on are unplanned, misplaced or misdefined. (1) Geometrization needs the Kneser-Milnor prime decomposition, which Layer 8 says 'is layer 1', but Layer 1 plans only connected sum: no prime or irreducible predicate and no existence or uniqueness theorem. (2) 'Seifert-fibered' is used as a JSJ condition but never defined (Seifert fibred spaces with exceptional fibres, and their base orbifolds). (3) Incompressible surfaces are planned twice, in Layer 7 ('Haken') and Layer 8 (incompressible tori), with no shared definition. (4) Layer 7 defines Haken as 'contains an incompressible surface', omitting irreducibility (and compactness and orientability), which the standard definition, and Yazdi's paper that the roadmap cites, require. (5) 'Atoroidal' has two inequivalent readings (Kirby's algebraic Z×Z condition, or 'every incompressible torus is boundary parallel'), and the layer fixes neither.

findings.fix: Create one owner for 3-manifold basics, either a new first sub-layer of Layer 8 or a Layer 7/8 shared node, with: embedded 2-spheres and irreducible, prime (with S^2 × S^1); the Kneser-Milnor prime decomposition (existence and uniqueness; Hatcher's 3M notes, Theorem 1.5); properly embedded two-sided surfaces, compressing discs, incompressible and ∂-incompressible surfaces; Haken := compact, orientable, irreducible and containing a two-sided incompressible surface; Seifert fibred spaces with their base orbifold and invariants; geometric atoroidality, with the algebraic version as a separate predicate and the comparison theorem. findings.claim: Layer 7 plans hyperbolic metrics 'on the model ℍⁿ' but never constructs ℍⁿ as a Riemannian manifold of curvature −1 or its isometry group, and does not reconcile with the hyperbolic planes already in the libraries, which use different normalisations. Mathlib's UpperHalfPlane metric, dist = 2 arsinh(|z−w|/(2√(Im z Im w))), is the curvature −1 metric |dz|/Im z. Tau Ceti's ConformalMapping hyperbolicDist on the disc is artanh‖z‖ from the origin, the metric |dz|/(1−|z|²) of curvature −4, which is half the curvature −1 distance. FuchsianOrbifolds Layer 2 must 'compare [UpperHalfPlane.volume] with hyperbolic Riemannian volume', which only Layer 7 supplies, and the atlas has no edge. Without a pinned model, Gauss-Bonnet areas and volume comparisons pick up factor-of-2 or factor-of-4 errors.

findings.claim: The Weeks target cannot be stated as sketched and its locator is wrong. hypVolume M takes a proof of Nonempty (HyperbolicMetric M), so 'hypVolume weeksManifold ≤ hypVolume M' needs a proof that the Weeks manifold is hyperbolic, for example an explicit face-pairing with the Poincaré polyhedron theorem in dimension 3, or a discrete group Γ ≤ PSL(2,ℂ) with ℍ³/Γ ≅ Weeks. No layer plans that, nor its orientability or closedness. Gabai-Meyerhoff-Milley also prove uniqueness, which the target omits. The references put 'the closed case (the Weeks manifold)' in arXiv:0910.5043, an expository survey; the theorem is in the JAMS paper arXiv:0705.4325, whose abstract states it.

findings.claim: Layer 10's cohomological inputs are misattributed or missing. (1) It takes 'singular and the implied de Rham / H² cohomology' from Mathlib, but Mathlib 082e2d3 has singular homology only. Singular cochains, cohomology, cup and cap products and fundamental classes are planned in AlgebraicTopology Stage 6 and the Euler characteristic in Stage 7, and no stage plans de Rham cohomology. (2) The Euler class of an oriented plane bundle is called 'a small standalone layer on top of Mathlib's bundle theory', but defining it needs the Thom class and Thom isomorphism of the disc bundle, or obstruction theory, or c_1 of the associated complex line bundle. None is planned, and Mathlib has no orientation of vector bundles. (3) 'An integrable subbundle of TM ... equivalently a maximal atlas of flat charts' is the Frobenius theorem, and Mathlib has no subbundle or distribution notion (it has the Lie bracket of vector fields). The atlas records none of these edges.

findings.claim: Zeeman's conjecture is a statement about polyhedra: a polyhedron is collapsible if some triangulation (cell structure) of it collapses, and collapsibility depends on the triangulation (there are non-collapsible simplicial 3-balls). The roadmap sketch and Tau Ceti's TauCeti.ZeemanConjecture both require one specific triangulation, the ordered 'staircase' cylinder on K, for every linear order, to collapse. That is a stronger statement, and could be false while Zeeman's conjecture is true. No equivalence between the two is cited.

Tau Ceti f790474 TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/SimplicialComplex/Zeeman.lean:124-127 'def ZeemanConjecture.{u} : Prop := ∀ (ι : Type u) [LinearOrder ι] (K : AbstractSimplicialComplex ι), K.Contractible2Complex → PreAbstractSimplicialComplex.Collapsible K.orderedCylinder.toPreAbstractSimplicialComplex' (docstring: 'The cylinder uses the staircase triangulation fixed by AbstractSimplicialComplex.orderedCylinder'). R. Kirby (ed.), Problems in Low-Dimensional Topology (version of 22 Dec 1995, the text published as AMS/IP Stud. Adv. Math. 2.2, 1997), https://math.berkeley.edu/~kirby/problems.ps.gz, read 2026-09-24, Problem 5.2 (p. 260): '(A) Zeeman Conjecture: K × I collapses to a point'. I. Dynnikov, arXiv:2608.23331v1 (HTML, read 2026-09-24): 'A polyhedron without a fixed cell structure is called collapsible if it admits a collapsible cell structure'; Conjecture 1.1 'Let K be a contractible compact two-dimensional polyhedron. Then K×[0;1] is collapsible.' Benedetti-Lutz, arXiv:1303.2070 (Electron. J. Combin. 20 (2013) P31): 'We construct the first explicit example of a simplicial 3-ball B_{15,66} that is not collapsible.'
findings.fix: Restate Layer 11's target, and give Tau Ceti a maintainer note to restate ZeemanConjecture, as: for every finite contractible 2-complex K, some subdivision of K.orderedCylinder (for instance an iterated stellar or barycentric subdivision, which Tau Ceti has) is collapsible, or equivalently some finite complex whose realization is PL homeomorphic to |K| × [0,1] collapses. Keep the ordered-cylinder statement as a separately named stronger variant, and add the non-collapsible 3-ball as a unit test that collapsibility is not a polyhedral invariant.

findings.claim: The unlock 'Conway mutation does not preserve concordance, [Kir97, 1.53]' is credited to Piccirillo's Conway/Kinoshita-Terasaka pair, but the list itself records the answer 'No' (Kearton 1989) for general mutation. Kirby notes that the orientation-preserving (positive) case was open. Kirk-Livingston then gave infinite families of knots not concordant to their positive mutants. Piccirillo's result is the finer smooth statement: a non-slice knot that is both topologically slice and a positive mutant of a slice knot. As stated (∃ K, ¬ Concordant K (mutate K)), the target's first proof is Kearton's.

findings.claim: F4.4 plans handleslide invariance 'via Perutz': 'the handleslid torus is Hamiltonian-isotopic, so invariance reduces to F3's continuation maps instead of a new (triangle) moduli problem'. That is not what Perutz proves, and it contradicts two other layers of the roadmap. (1) Perutz's Hamiltonian isotopy exists only for Kähler forms omega_lambda (class eta + lambda theta, lambda > 0) for which the Heegaard tori are Lagrangian. It also needs gamma_0 and gamma_1 to meet in exactly two transverse points, an area constraint on the surface, and the basepoint z outside the handlesliding region. F4.1 tells the builder the opposite: 'T_alpha is only ever needed totally real ... do not chase Lagrangian-ness'. (2) Perutz's continuation maps live in monotone Lagrangian Floer theory with minimal Maslov index 2, where discs do bubble off and are cancelled by OS Theorem 3.15. F3 plans only the exact case ('exactness kills bubbling outright') and says 'Skip monotone Floer theory entirely'. (3) The energy bound for his continuation strips is derived from finiteness of holomorphic-triangle classes (OS §9.2), and the maps are continuation maps of Hamiltonian fibrations (Seidel). Neither is in F3. (4) The isotopy itself is built from symplectic sums and nodal degenerations of symmetric products, relative Hilbert schemes and flux (Perutz §§2-5), none of which any layer plans. (5) The triangle moduli problem is not avoided anyway. F4.5's cobordism maps, exact triangles and JTZ naturality all use Ozsváth-Szabó's triangle maps, and Perutz says his maps agree with them only through a gluing theorem for holomorphic sections.
findings.evidence: T. Perutz, 'Hamiltonian handleslides for Heegaard Floer homology', arXiv:0801.0564v2 (https://arxiv.org/abs/0801.0564, TeX source read 2026-09-24). Theorem 1.2: 'Assume that gamma_0 cap gamma_1 is a transverse intersection consisting of precisely two points ... (2) T_0 is Hamiltonian-isotopic to T_1 if and only if int_D alpha = (1+lambda) int_A alpha - 2 lambda.' Corollary 1.3: 'Assume that z lies outside the handlesliding region. Then there is a canonical isomorphism HF^+(alpha, beta, s) -> HF^+(alpha', beta, s)'. §6: 'Having an a priori bound on area is essential for compactness, and for this reason it is important to work with Lagrangian (not merely totally real) submanifolds'; 'Heegaard tori are monotone Lagrangians of minimal Maslov index 2. The troublesome feature of Lagrangian Floer theory in such a case is that bubbling-off of discs spoils compactness ... they always do so in cancelling pairs [OS, Theorem 3.15]'; 'According to [OS, Section 9.2], the number of finite-energy holomorphic triangles T satisfying these conditions is finite'; Remark: 'The continuation isomorphisms ... are the same as the isomorphisms constructed by Ozsváth-Szabó using holomorphic triangles. To see this one applies a gluing theorem for holomorphic sections'. Stage F4.1: '⚠ T_alpha is only ever needed totally real (with a taming form); do not chase Lagrangian-ness.' Lane F3: 'exactness kills bubbling outright ... ⚠ Skip monotone Floer theory entirely'. Juhász-Thurston-Zemke arXiv:1210.4996v4 §1.2: 'The first step towards naturality was made by Ozsváth and Szabó [HolDiskFour, Theorem 2.1], who constructed maps Psi ...' (built from triangle maps) and 'One has to prove that HF has no monodromy around the simple handleswap loop'.

findings.claim: F2.3 limits compactness to 'fixed genus-zero domains only; resist the general theory', and the README says the Sym^g route has a 'fixed strip domain, genus-zero disk-tree bubbling only ... no Deligne-Mumford'. The Ozsváth-Szabó proofs of F4.4 and F4.5 targets need two compactness-and-gluing problems outside that scope. (a) Holomorphic rectangles with varying conformal structure. The disk with four boundary punctures has a one-parameter conformal modulus, and its two ends break the rectangle into pairs of triangles. This gives associativity of triangle maps (OS Theorem 8.16), which proves handleslide invariance (Theorem 9.5 via Lemma 9.6). It also gives the composition laws of cobordism maps and the null-homotopies in the surgery exact sequences (square counts in OS math/0105202 §9). (b) Neck stretching. Sigma' = Sigma #_T E degenerates to Sigma v E as T -> infinity, and the target Sym^{g+1}(Sigma #_T E) degenerates with it; the argument needs Gromov compactness and gluing to spheres in Sym^2(E). This is OS's proof of stabilization invariance (§10), which F4.4 lists on the v3 path, and of the triangle gluing across Sigma # E (math/0105202 Theorem 9.4) used in the exact sequences. F2.5 plans gluing only for broken strips and bubbles (Schwarz; McDuff-Salamon Chapter 10). As scoped, v3 (HF-hat with stabilization invariance) cannot be completed.
findings.evidence: Ozsváth-Szabó arXiv:math/0101206v4 (https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0101206, TeX source read 2026-09-24; theorem numbers computed from the source), §8.4: 'Let R denote the "rectangle": the unit disk with four marked boundary points ... We would like to count pseudo-holomorphic maps of the rectangle in Sym^g(Sigma) (without fixing the conformal structure of the domain) ... there is another type of end not encountered before in the counts of triangles, arising from the non-compactness of Mod(R) = R. As this parameter goes to +-infinity, the corresponding rectangle breaks up conformally into a pair of triangles'. §9, proof of Lemma 9.6: 'The result is now a direct application of Theorem 8.16'. §10: '... which we can view as a subset of Sym^{g+1}(Sigma v E), which in turn can be thought of as a degenerated version of Sym^{g+1}(Sigma') ... A Gromov compactness argument shows that for sufficiently large T, all of the moduli spaces ... lie in the domain of this gluing map'; 'the degeneration of Sigma' above is closely related to the degenerations studied by Ionel-Parker and Li-Ruan' (Theorem 10.4, Proposition 10.15, Lemmas 10.17-10.18). arXiv:math/0105202, Theorem 9.4: 'We will form the connected sum Sigma # E ... we have a diffeomorphism of moduli spaces M(psi') = M(psi) x M(psi_0)'. findings.claim: The roadmap states that 'Némethi's H^- computes the holomorphic HF^- of every plumbed 3-manifold', with dependencies 'the staged HF^-/HF^infinity flavors of F4.5 and the combinatorial Lane L'. The cited theorem says something narrower, and its proof needs inputs that no layer plans. (i) Zemke proves it for plumbings of a tree of disk bundles over S^2. Plumbing graphs with cycles, and plumbings with higher-genus bases, are excluded, so 'every plumbed 3-manifold' is false as a statement of the cited result. (ii) The isomorphism is with the U-completed HF^-, an F[[U]]-module, not with HF^-. This loses nothing for rational homology spheres or torsion spin^c structures, but those are the only cases Zemke says so for. (iii) It is relatively graded only when b_1(Y(G)) = 0. Compatibility with the Lambda^*(H_1/Tors) action is Zemke's Conjecture 1.2, not a theorem. (iv) Zemke uses the Ozsváth-Stipsicz-Szabó homological lattice complex, defined for arbitrary plumbing trees. CHF Lane L builds 'Némethi's lattice (co)homology', whose definition 'was most naturally stated for negative definite manifolds', so a comparison is needed. (v) The proof runs through the Manolescu-Ozsváth link surgery formula (arXiv:1011.1317) and Zemke's bordered link-surgery modules (arXiv:2109.11520). Neither is planned anywhere in the atlas; F4.5 supplies only the flavors.
findings.evidence: I. Zemke, arXiv:2111.14962v4 (Duke Math. J., accepted version; https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.14962, TeX source read 2026-09-24). Abstract: 'if Y is a 3-manifold which is the boundary of a plumbing of a tree of disk bundles over S^2, then the lattice homology of Y coincides with the Heegaard Floer homology of Y'. Theorem 1.1: 'If G is a plumbing tree, then there is an isomorphism of F[[U]]-modules HF(G) = HF^-(Y(G)) [bold, completed]. When b_1(Y(G))=0, the isomorphism is relatively graded.' Also: 'we write HF^-(Y(G)) for the F[[U]] module obtained by completing HF^-(Y(G)) with respect to the U action'; 'Our proof of Theorem 1.1 uses the link surgery formula of Manolescu and Ozsváth ... using the techniques of the author [ZemBordered = arXiv:2109.11520]'; 'his definition was most naturally stated for negative definite manifolds. Ozsváth, Stipsicz and Szabó gave a homological definition of lattice complex which is defined for arbitrary plumbing trees ... In this paper, we focus on the description given by Ozsváth, Stipsicz and Szabó'; 'we are not able to prove that our isomorphism intertwines this homology action when b_1(Y)>0' (Conjecture 1.2). HF README line 273: 'holomorphic HF^- of every plumbed 3-manifold'. CHF README lines 58-60: 'Zemke's theorem ... that it computes HF^- of all plumbed manifolds'. data/atlas.json: no stage mentions a link surgery formula.

findings.claim: Reconciliations 1 and 3 both rest on multi-pointed Heegaard Floer homology, which no layer plans. For reconciliation 1, the appendix of Ozsváth-Stipsicz-Szabó identifies the homology of a convenient multi-pointed diagram with HF-hat(Y) tensor (F+F)^{b(D)-1}. It does so through the multi-pointed theory of Ozsváth-Szabó's link paper (Theorem 4.5), Lipshitz's index theorem, the Sarkar-Wang classification of positive index-one domains, and the polygon count. For reconciliation 3, Manolescu-Ozsváth-Sarkar compute knot Floer homology from a 2n-pointed torus diagram, through Proposition 2.3 (the extra-basepoints proposition). No layer plans multi-pointed diagrams, their complexes over F[U_1,...,U_l], invariance under adding basepoint pairs, or the HF-hat tensor V^{l-1} theorem. F5 names only 'Knot Floer homology via doubly-pointed diagrams'; CHF H.1 plans only the combinatorics of multi-pointed diagrams. The published proofs of the multi-pointed invariance results do their gluing in Lipshitz's cylindrical setting. So reconciliation 1's stated dependency list, 'F4.4 (stabilization and diagram-move invariance) and the combinatorial Lane H', is incomplete: it also needs the multi-pointed theory and hence F5-level analysis.

findings.claim: F1.2 states 'The Calderón-Zygmund inequality ||u||_{W^{1,p}} <= C||dbar u||_{L^p} via the Cauchy kernel' with no hypothesis on u or p, and it is false as written. Any holomorphic u on a disk or strip, for example u = 1, has dbar u = 0 and ||u||_{W^{1,p}} > 0. Two hypotheses are missing. First, compact support: u in C_0^infinity or W^{1,p}_0 of the open domain, or else a lower-order term C||u||_{L^p} on the right together with shrinking to an interior subdomain. The boundary version for totally real boundary conditions also carries the lower-order term. Second, 1 < p < infinity: the Beurling (Cauchy-kernel) transform, which carries dbar u to du, is a Calderón-Zygmund operator and is unbounded on L^1 and L^infinity.
findings.evidence: Stage F1.2 text: '2. The Calderón-Zygmund inequality ||u||_{W^{1,p}} <= C||dbar u||_{L^p} via the Cauchy kernel; interior elliptic bootstrapping; boundary regularity for totally real boundary conditions (Schwarz reflection).' Counterexample: u = 1 on the unit disk, so dbar u = 0 while ||u||_{W^{1,p}} = pi^{1/p}. The PDE roadmap's own warning, confirmed in RT-AREA-pde: 'A CZ operator is not bounded on L^1 or L^infinity'. Neither Mathlib 082e2d3 nor Tau Ceti f790474 has a Calderón-Zygmund or Beurling-transform declaration (AUDIT-40 B-10, pending review, 'No notion of a CZ kernel exists').
findings.fix: Restate F1.2 as three targets. (a) For 1 < p < infinity and u in C_0^infinity(C, C^n): ||du||_{L^p} <= c_p ||dbar u||_{L^p}, from the L^p boundedness of the Beurling transform; so for u in W^{1,p}_0(Omega) with Omega bounded, ||u||_{W^{1,p}} <= C(p, Omega) ||dbar u||_{L^p}. (b) The interior estimate ||u||_{W^{1,p}(Omega')} <= C(||dbar u||_{L^p(Omega)} + ||u||_{L^p(Omega)}) for Omega' compactly contained in Omega. (c) Its half-disk version with totally real boundary conditions, with the same lower-order term. Record u = 1 as the regression test.

The first Chern class c_1(s), the Euler class of the orthogonal plane field, enters strong admissibility (OS Definition 4.10), which HF^+-, HF^- and HF^infinity for non-torsion spin^c need. No atlas layer plans parallelizability of 3-manifolds or the obstruction theory. Poincaré duality is AlgebraicTopology Stage 6 and the Euler class of oriented plane bundles is GeometricTopology Layer 10, but no stage edge records either.

(c) c_1(Sym^g(Sigma)) = U - sum mu(A_i)mu(B_i) (Lemma 2.8, quoted from Macdonald), which gives Mas(phi + S) = Mas(phi) + 2 (Lemma 3.3) and is needed once sphere bubbles matter in F4.5. findings.claim: F3 plans Floer homology of 'exact Lagrangians in an exact symplectic manifold (zero section vs its Hamiltonian image in T*S^1, then T*M)', with 'HF(L, phi(L)) = H_*(L)-type computations in cotangent bundles'. The standard setting needs an extra hypothesis that F3 does not state: a Liouville manifold (or domain) with an almost complex structure of contact type (convex) at infinity, and a maximum principle, or Hamiltonians with compact support. findings.claim: F4.5 stages 'orientation systems and Z' before 'naturality (JTZ) as the capstone', and the standing conventions ask that every F_2 theorem be stated so that 'the coefficient ring can be generalized without restating the geometry'. Over Z, the literature currently gives only projective naturality, well defined up to an overall sign (Gartner, AGT 2023, whose accepted version reworked unsound arguments). findings.claim: The acceptance check '`HF-hat(L(p,q))` over F_2 from the genus-1 diagram (every moduli count a bigon) gives F^p' is mis-stated, and it cannot rule out a vacuous definition. In the standard genus-1 diagram the p intersection points lie in p different Spin^c structures, so pi_2(x,y) is empty for x != y and the differential is zero for purely topological reasons: no moduli space is counted. The same holds for 'the first seam crossed end to end'. Any definition with the right generators and Spin^c splitting passes both checks, whatever its holomorphic counts are.
findings.evidence: OS arXiv:math/0105202, Proposition 3.1 (HF-hat(L(p,q),s) = Z for each s), proof: 'Consider the genus one Heegaard splitting of Y. Here we can arrange for alpha to meet beta in precisely p points. Each intersection point corresponds to a different SpinC structure, and, of course, all boundary maps are trivial.' OS math/0101206v4 Proposition 2.15: 'if epsilon(x,y) != 0, then pi_2(x,y) is empty'.
findings.fix: Keep the L(p,q) check as a Spin^c and generator test, and add two checks that exercise holomorphic counts. (1) HF-hat(S^3) = F from a genus-1 diagram in which beta is isotoped to meet alpha in three points: one cancelling pair, whose index-one bigon must count 1 mod 2. (2) HF-hat(S^1 x S^2) = F^2 from the weakly admissible genus-1 diagram with two intersection points and two bigons, which cancel mod 2 (OS math/0105202 §3). Correct 'every moduli count a bigon' to 'no nonconstant moduli space occurs'.

findings.claim: Two locators are imprecise. (a) F4 cites 'Ozsváth-Szabó (arXiv:math/0101206) §§2-4', but F4.4's invariance items are in §6 (J-independence), §7 (isotopies), §§8-9 (triangles and handleslides) and §10 (stabilization), with §11 concluding. (b) F4.3 cites 'admissibility energy bounds (OS Lemmas 4.12-4.13)'. In arXiv v4 the energy bound is Lemma 3.5. Lemma 4.12 characterizes weak admissibility for all Spin^c structures by an area form, Lemma 4.13 is finiteness under weak admissibility, and finiteness under strong admissibility (needed for HF^- and HF^infinity) is Lemma 4.14. Admissibility gives finiteness of positive classes, not energy bounds.
